chunks: My father and Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari (may Allāh have mercy on him) narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Al-Ḥasan, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥurayz, from someone who informed him, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to my mosque, the Mosque of Qubā, and prays two Rak’ah in it, will return with the reward of an ‘Umrah.

key_terms.عُمْرَةٍ: Umrah, a minor pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ قُبَا: Mosque of Qubā, the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.) in Medina

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying two Rak'ah in the Mosque of Qubā?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the Mosque of Qubā as a site of significant spiritual merit, equating the reward of two rak'ahs of prayer there to that of an 'Umrah. This comparison highlights the unique status of Qubā, the first mosque built by the Prophet (saww) upon his migration to Medina, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of specific locations tied to the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet's life.
